topic.title: Passing Objects to Methods
topic.description: How objects are passed to methods

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how objects travel between methods in Java? Let's break it down!

• How Java passes objects to methods (it's not what you think!)
• The difference between passing objects vs. primitive types
• How to modify objects inside methods safely

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're at a library. You don't carry the actual book around - you just show your library card (reference) to access it. That's exactly how Java passes objects!

When you pass an object to a method:
• You're actually passing a *reference* (like a library card) to the object
• The method can use this reference to interact with the original object
• Changes made inside the method affect the original object

This is different from primitive types (like `int` or `double`), which are passed by *value* - like making a photocopy of a page instead of showing your library card.

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: When an object is passed to a method, the reference value is copied (pass-by-value of reference)
The method can modify the object's state through the copied reference
Changes to the object's fields inside the method persist after the method returns
Reassigning the parameter to a new object inside the method does not affect the caller
Arrays of objects are also passed by reference value, so element modifications are visible

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Objects are passed by reference - methods work with the original object. Primitives are passed by value - methods get a copy. Practice creating and modifying objects through methods.

questions.question: When an object is passed to a method in Java, what is actually passed?
options: A copy of the entire object
A copy of the reference to the object
questions.explanation: When an object is passed to a method, a copy of the reference (memory address) is passed. This means the method can modify the object's state through the reference.

questions.question: If a method changes the data fields of a passed object, is the original object affected?
options: Yes, because the method has a reference to the same object
Only if the object is declared final
questions.explanation: Since the method receives a reference to the same object, any changes to the object's data fields inside the method affect the original object.
